We denote probabilities with P and PDFs with . They are related via integration: P(x ∈ [x1, x2]|I) = ∫ x2 x1 dx (x|I). Note that proba- bilities take values in P ∈ [0, 1], whereas PDFs in  ∈ ℝ+ 0 = [0, ∞]. Bayes’ theorem applies to both, so that a strict discrimination be- tween those is not always necessary. We therefore use the word “probability” for both, probabilities and PDFs.

In case Δ𝜇+, Δ𝜆+ are not integer numbers, a slightly more sophisticated argumentation leads to exactly the same result: Agent b assumes that a’s past belief, which has lead to ΔJ+, was based on some eﬀective, accumulated data d′ and hap- pened according to Bayes’ rule. This implies (xc|d′, Ibac) = (d′|xc, Ibac)(xc|Ibac)∕(d′|Ibac) and means that the data d′ must have been such that (d′|xc, Ibac) ∝ xΔ𝜇+ c (1 − xc)Δ𝜆+ . This should therefore also be the likelihood (ΔJ+|xc, Ibc) that agent b uses for the update. This leads to Equation (A22 )as well.

Actually, since a self-statement is self-referential with respect to its truth value, a logically fully consistent update would require to solve an implicit self-consistent relation. This can be seen for example in case agent a makes the statement to be a notorious liar, which if true is contradicted by just have made an honest confession. We, as well as our agents, do not invest mental energy in such philosophical calculations, but just use the pragmatic Equation (A28).

Cheap talk is characterized by being costless, non- binding, and unveriﬁable.[29] The ﬁrst condition is not fulﬁlled in our reputation game as there communication opportunities are a valuable resource for the agents.
Human reputation and self-esteem are certainly more complex phenomena.

We denote probabilities with P and PDFs with . They are related via integration: P(x ∈ [x1, x2]|I) = ∫ x2 x1 dx (x|I). Note that proba- bilities take values in P ∈ [0, 1], whereas PDFs in  ∈ ℝ+ 0 = [0, ∞]. Bayes’ theorem applies to both, so that a strict discrimination be- tween those is not always necessary. We therefore use the word “probability” for both, probabilities and PDFs.
